This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 to 3 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH5 2.

The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 14.03.2022 at about 4.30 p.m. he had been riding Honda Deo bearing Reg.No.TN22BR4135 near HP Petrol Bunk, 1st Main Road,
Rajagopalanagar, Bengaluru, a BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA01F8988 proceeding infront of his motor cycle slow down and stopped, as a result he also slow down his motor cycle, at that time,
tempo traveller bearing Reg.No.KA01AF8605 came in high speed rash and negligently and dashed against his motor cycle from back side, as a result he dashed to the BMTC bus from behind.
Due to the impact of the accident, he fell down and sustained major fractures and his motor cycle is also fully damaged.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Sri Sai Kanva Hospital Bengaluru, after first aid shifted to Sparsh Hospital Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment SCCH5 as indoor patient and spent an amount of Rs.10,00,000/ towards medical expenses,
Rs.1,00,000/ towards transportation and nourishing food and he has to spend another Rs.3,00,000/ for future medical expenses.

3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 49 years, hale and healthy, working as Deputy Manager in private company, thereby earning Rs.99,175/ p.m., due to this accident, he cannot work as earlier and he has lost his income and earning capacity.

Out of this accident crime No.38/2022 is registered against driver of the tempo traveller bearing Reg.No.KA01AF8605 before the Peenya Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC.
R1 is the insurer, R2 is owner of the tempo traveller, R3 is internal insurer of the BMTC bus, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and SCCH5 grant compensation of Rs.60,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.

On service of notice, R1/insurer of the tempo traveller bearing Reg.No.KA01AF8605 has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner, admitted issuance of insurance policy to the said tempo traveller, further submitted that, accident is occurred only due to negligency of driver of the BMTC bus, who suddenly stopped his vehicle without giving any Padam Raj Bhatt vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164023847/
2 indications to the vehicle coming behind.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in them va that occurred on 14.03.2022 at about 4.30 p.m. when petitioner was returning from his work from Hegganahalli on Honda Dio bearing Reg.No.TN22BR4135, near HP Petrol Bunk, 1st Main Road, Rajagopalanagar, Bengaluru, at that time, one BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA01F8988 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed to the petitioner and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

On the other hand, R1 has deposed his evidence as RW1 and marked 1 document as per Ex.R.1.
Further driver of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA01F8988 is examined as RW2 and closed his evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:

he dashed his motor cycle against hind portion of the bus.

Further admits that, bus was constantly moving.
There is no negligency of the bus driver, very accident is occurred only due to negligency of the Tempo Traveller.
12. On the other hand, R1/insurer of the Tempo Traveller has deposed his evidence as RW1 and SCCH5 furnished copy of insurance policy marked as Ex.R.1.
In chiefexamination deposed that,
very accident
is occurred due to negligency of the driver of BMTC bus and there is no negligency of the Tempo Traveller driver.

Further admits that, charge sheet is filed only against Tempo Traveller bearing Reg.No.KA01AF8605.
Further denied that, he is deposing false evidence.
He has seen the police papers.
He has denied that, as per the police papers there is no negligency of the bus driver.

13. 14. In crossexamination by counsel for petitioner admits that, very accident is occurred only due to negligency of the driver of the Tempo Traveller and there is no his negligency.
Even in cross examination by counsel for R1 he has reiterated the said facts.

15. Police papers marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8 speaks that, entire accident is occurred only due to negligency of driver of the the Tempo Traveller, on a public road Tempo Traveller came in high speed, dashed against the motor cycle, ridden by the petitioner, ultimately very motor cycle dashed on hind portion of the SCCH5 bus, so that, petitioner has sustained injuries and taken treatment at Sparsh Hospital.

Looking to the facts of this case, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the Tempo Traveller and there is no negligency of the bus driver and petitioner.
Out of the very accident, petitioner has sustained injuries and taken treatment.
Further this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, evidence available on record is sufficient to hold that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour against the Tempo Traveller.
Hence, I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained segmental fracture of right femur, comminuted segmental fracture of right patella with MCL ligament complex injury, fracture head of SCCH5 fibula left, fracture inferior glenoid fracture right, left sided rib fracture 3 - 6, 5 th rib fracture right, pubic rami fracture, for which he has undergone DFN right femur+TBW+encerclage+partial patellectomy.

In this regard he has produced copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.6 issued by Sparsh Hosptial wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 14.03.2022 to 29.03.2022, Xray Films marked as Ex.P.13.
17.

Insupport of his case Incharge Medical Record Office at Sparsha Hospital is examined as PW2 who has furnished authorization letter marked as Ex.P.14, copy of MLC extract marked as Ex.P.15,
copy of police intimation is marked as Ex.P. 16, inpatient case sheet is marked as Ex.P.17.
SCCH5 18.

19. In crossexamination admits that, he has not treated the petitioner, there is every chance of further improvement in mobility and stability with regular use of the limbs and follow up treatment.
He has assessed only physical disability.
Further denied that, assessment made by him is higher side.

As per the medical records marked at Ex.P.6 discharge summary, Ex.P.7 wound certificate,
Ex.P.11 medical bills it is noticed that, he has taken treatment at Sparsh Hospital since 14.03.2022 to 29.03.2022, surgery is conducted on right femur SCCH5 segmental area, as per say of the Padam Raj Bhatt vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164023847/

In crossexamination PW1 admits that, as on today his monthly salary is 89,175/ getting through his account and working for the said company.

Under such circumstances, it is clear that,
there is no loss of future income, but as per the answer given in the cross examination he was on leave for 3 months.

Further for travelling he has spent Rs.600/ per day to reach his office, further for sending the children to school spent Rs.4,000/ p.m. as a rent, to prove the said fact he has not furnished any documents about the vehicle charges.

Further in crossexamination admitted that,
his medical bills of Rs.4,85,836/ is reimbursed from his Medi Assist SCCH5 Company.
Under such circumstances, he is not entitled for the said bills.
He has furnished remaining bill of Rs.1,06,269/ he is entitled for the said bill.
In this regard, there is no dispute by counsel for respondents.
Considering the same, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, there is no functional disability.
Hence petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head loss on account of future income.

21. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 49 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.9, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner is 24.10.1972 and the alleged accident is occurred on 14.03.2022, accordingly relying on Ex.P.9 his age is considered about 50 years as on the date of accident.
SCCH5 22.

As per his case, he was working as Deputy Manager in private Company, thereby drawing salary of Rs.99,175/ p.m. to prove the said fact, he has furnished payslips marked as Ex.P.10 issued by Credo Brands Marketing Private Limited.

23. Keeping in mind injuries caused to the petitioner, treatment taken, expenses incurred and also the pain suffered, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to allot compensation under other heads, accordingly for pain and sufferings compensation of Rs.20,000/
is awarded, for conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges Rs.20,000/ is awarded, for loss of amenities of life Rs.20,000/ is awarded, further he is entitled for Rs.2,79,825/ towards loss of income during laid up period i.e., 3 months take home salary.

Further petitioner is also entitled for SCCH5 compensation for medical expenses incurred by him, for which, he has produced medical bills marked as Ex.P.11 for an amount of Rs.1,06,269/, medical prescriptions are marked as Ex.P.12.
24.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,46,094/ with SCCH5 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

26. In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the insurer of the tempo traveller bearing Reg.No.KA01AF 8605 has issued insurance policy bearing No.10003/31/22/163727 which is valid for the period from 11.09.2021 to 10.09.2022, the alleged accident was occurred on 14.03.2022, it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Further there is no dispute about driving license of driver of offending vehicle i.e., tempo traveller so that,
R1/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
R3 is not liable to pay any compensation.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
SCCH5 27. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,46,094/ (Rupees Four Lakhs Forty Six Thousand Ninety Four Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through epayment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
SCCH5 The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
